en.name: Sumac, ground
en.summary: Ground sumac keeps about 6 months in an airtight jar in a dark, dry cupboard away from heat. Nothing unsafe happens after that — a dried, ground berry is far too dry for microbes — but the deep wine-red colour and the lemony acidity both fade, and those are the entire reason to own it.
en.pantry: 6 months in an airtight jar, in the dark, away from the steam and heat of the hob. Sumac is the clearest case in the spice rack of colour telling you the truth: fresh sumac is a deep wine red and tastes sharply lemony, while faded brick-brown sumac has lost the acid and tastes of little except salt. It clumps in a humid kitchen because the ground berry is naturally slightly moist and sticky, so break up the lumps with a fork rather than assuming the jar has gone bad. Many brands are salted, which does nothing at all for keeping quality.
en.fridge: There is no refrigerated timeline for ground sumac and no need for one. A cold jar collects condensation every time it comes out of the fridge, and damp is what makes sumac cake and eventually mould. Keep it in the cupboard. The exception is a large catering bag you will be working through for a year or more, which is better sealed tightly and kept somewhere cool and dark than opened repeatedly in a hot kitchen.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists for ground sumac, and freezing is not worth doing. The problem it would solve — oxidation of colour and aroma — is better solved by buying small jars often, and each trip out of the freezer invites the condensation that turns a free-flowing powder into a brick.
spoilage: Colour faded from deep wine red to dull brick or brown.
No sour, lemony hit on the tongue when you taste a pinch.
Hard cakes that will not break up, a sign it has taken on moisture.
Visible mould or a musty smell in a jar stored somewhere damp.
tips: Buy it in small quantities and often; sumac is bought for colour and acid, both of which fade.
Judge the jar by colour before you judge it by date.
Never dip a wet or oily spoon into the jar.
Add it at the end of cooking or as a finishing sprinkle — heat drives off the sourness.

faq.q: How long does ground sumac last?
faq.a: About 6 months in an airtight jar in a dark, dry cupboard. It stays safe much longer than that, but the colour and the lemony acidity fade.

faq.q: How can you tell if sumac has gone bad?
faq.a: By colour and taste rather than by date. Deep wine red and sharply sour is good; dull brown and merely salty means it has nothing left to give.

faq.q: Does sumac need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. The fridge adds condensation every time the jar comes out, and damp is what makes sumac cake and mould. A dark, dry cupboard is better.

zh.name: 鹽膚木粉
zh.summary: 鹽膚木粉裝在密封罐、放在陰暗乾燥、遠離爐火的櫃子裡，大約可放 6 個月。過了之後不會變得不安全——乾燥的果粉太乾，微生物根本長不起來——但那抹酒紅色和檸檬般的酸味會一起褪掉，而那正是買它的全部理由。
zh.pantry: 密封罐、避光、遠離爐台的蒸氣與熱源，6 個月。在整個香料櫃裡，鹽膚木粉是「顏色就是答案」最清楚的例子：新鮮的是深酒紅色，嚐起來有明亮的酸；褪成磚褐色之後酸就沒了，只剩鹹味。它在潮濕的廚房裡會結塊，因為磨碎的果實本身就帶點濕潤黏性，所以看到結塊先用叉子壓散，不要直接判它死刑。市售品很多有加鹽，那對保存完全沒有幫助。
zh.fridge: 鹽膚木粉沒有冷藏期限，也不需要。冰過的罐子每次拿出來都會結露，而濕氣正是讓它結塊、最後長霉的原因，放櫃子就好。唯一的例外是那種要用上一年以上的大包裝，與其在熱廚房裡反覆開闔，不如密封好、收在陰涼避光的地方。
zh.freezer: 鹽膚木粉沒有任何冷凍期限，也不值得冷凍。冷凍想解決的問題是顏色與香氣的氧化，而那個問題用「少量勤買」解決得更好；每進出冷凍一次，就多一次結露的機會，把原本鬆散的粉變成一塊磚。
spoilage: 顏色從深酒紅褪成暗磚色或褐色。
捏一點嚐嚐，完全沒有那股檸檬般的酸。
結成壓不散的硬塊，表示它吸了水。
放在潮濕處的罐子裡看得到霉，或聞起來有霉味。
tips: 少量勤買；買鹽膚木粉買的是顏色和酸味，這兩樣都會褪。
絕對不要把沾濕或沾油的湯匙伸進罐子裡。
起鍋前或上桌前再撒——加熱會把酸味趕走。

faq.a: 密封罐放在陰暗乾燥的櫃子裡大約 6 個月。安全上可以放更久，但顏色和檸檬般的酸味會褪掉。

faq.q: 怎麼知道鹽膚木粉壞了？
faq.a: 看顏色和嚐味道，不是看日期。深酒紅、嚐起來夠酸就是好的；暗褐色、只剩鹹味就表示它已經沒東西可以給了。
不用。罐子每次從冰箱拿出來都會結露，而濕氣正是讓它結塊、長霉的元凶。陰暗乾燥的櫃子更好。
